briefing.text: A tumour-normal somatic MAF normally has germline variants filtered out (normal alt reads ~0), so counting pathogenic variants in data_mutations.txt measures somatic prevalence, not germline carrier prevalence. Tabulate n_alt_count/n_ref_count and Mutation_Status first. If germline calls are not deposited, do not treat the somatic count as a germline rate. Under the benchmark convention a hypothesis about this cohort's germline findings gets True or False, not Not verifiable, even when germline calls are missing; decide it from the study design and established biology, and say which kind of evidence decided the label.
briefing.reason: This is the main trap. A naive count of the MAF would give a misleadingly low 'germline' rate, and missing germline data could wrongly push the team toward Not verifiable.

briefing.text: If you try to identify germline variants, use allele counts in the matched normal (e.g. normal VAF > 0.2 = germline evidence). Tumour VAF near 0.5 or 1.0 is not proof of germline status, because LOH and high purity produce the same pattern.
briefing.reason: Without this, the team might call germline carriers from tumour VAF, which misclassifies somatic variants.

briefing.text: Germline prevalence depends on the definition: count only Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic variants (ACMG/AMP) in a standard cancer-predisposition gene list (e.g. ACMG-59 or ~100 predisposition genes) and exclude VUS. Adding VUS inflates the rate; using only a few genes deflates it. State the gene list and classification you used.
briefing.reason: The 5% threshold is sensitive to the definition, so it must be explicit.

briefing.text: Compute prevalence per patient: carriers divided by all unique sequenced patients with matched normals (the library reports ~500 samples, all SOMATIC_STATUS=Matched; verify this). Do not use only the patients who appear in the variant file as the denominator.
briefing.reason: A wrong denominator shifts a rate measured against a 5% threshold.

briefing.text: Reference values from established literature: in large studies of patients with advanced or metastatic cancer sequenced with matched normals, P/LP germline variants in cancer-predisposition genes are reported in about 8-17% of patients (Huang 2018 Cell PanCanAtlas ~8%; Mandelker 2017 JAMA ~17.5%; Schrader 2016 JAMA Oncol ~16%). Confirm the cohort type (cancer types, SAMPLE_TYPE, SOMATIC_STATUS) before applying these values. If the tables cannot count germline variants directly, use them as the established-biology benchmark. The library cited these from memory and did not verify them.
briefing.reason: If germline calls are absent, the team needs an external benchmark for the established-biology route the task allows.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed the deposited MAF is somatic-only (normal VAF scan, empty Mutation_Status). From that they concluded the label must come from recall of the source study's reported germline rate (~12%). Neither tested whether that recalled figure uses the same denominator (all 500 cases vs a subset) and the same variant definition ('putative pathogenic' vs strictly P/LP) as the hypothesis.
Both assumed the hypothesis is about this study (a metastatic pan-cancer cohort with matched normals) rather than one attached from another publication.
unused_evidence: data_clinical_patient.txt column 'Other Cancer History': about 25 patients have prior or multiple cancers, including one 'Bilateral Retinoblastoma', a classic hereditary presentation. This is a phenotypic proxy for germline predisposition that neither team tabulated.

In predisposition genes, the MAF columns Freq_ExAC, dbSNP_RS and n_alt_count/n_ref_count were only screened with a high normal-VAF cutoff. Neither team looked for indirect germline-linked signals, such as somatic second hits or LOH in BRCA1/2, RB1 or TP53 in patients with multiple cancers.
data_cna_hg19.seg (LOH at predisposition loci) and data_sv.txt were not used.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the same weakest point: the label rests on recalling the published germline rate. Both only reported it, and neither looked for any in-data corroboration, however indirect.
second_readings: 'Putative pathogenic germline variants' could mean a broader putative class or a strict P/LP set. The reported percentage depends on the definition, though the plausible readings of the source finding both exceed 5%.
'Cases' could mean all 500 sequenced patients or only those with germline analysis. A different denominator would shift the percentage.
challenge.verdict: High trust in 'False'. The hypothesis plainly concerns this matched-normal metastatic cohort. Both teams correctly found that the tables hold no germline calls, and the study's published germline rate (about 12%) is well above 5%. The only weakness is that both teams rest on the same recalled figure, with no corroboration from the data.
